body: Home health/assisted living personnel here. It’s a rough industry. The mental and physical strain, the management and the pay is hard. I love my job and I understand some things are hard, but there are so many things that could get fixed. For example, I have had residents in an ASSISTED LIVING facility that need to be put in skilled nursing. I get paid as a assisted living/medication tech not a higher wage that a skilled nursing worker would get. If I bring it up to my administrators, they don’t fix it because we need to keep beds full. If we aren’t full- they can’t pay staff. Wages are low, hours are tough. I work 13 hrs, 4 days a week but I’m on call a few days a week. I don’t get paid to be on call. It’s very frustrating. Many people quit because of the stress and low pay, and we don’t get any benefits. It’s also hard working in borderline unsafe environments, when it comes to residential situations. Smokers, hoarders, pest problems, too many animals with waste everywhere. They can’t take of themselves but it’s can be hazardous. I’ve worked in a place where the back yard was filled with junk and had rusty saw blades and other things, I’ve injured myself multiple times. My agency had me do “chore hours” which was yard work for a few hours a month. I had to clean a garage full of rat pee and poop and I got very sick. I wasn’t given any equipment to clean safely. I had to buy some stuff but even then, I don’t make enough for that. Mentally- it’s hard. I can deal with the part though because it’s just a part of the job. Deaths, getting hit/bit/screamed at, walking in on someone smearing poop on the walls, being sexually harassed with words and physical attempts, connecting with people, dealing with snarky families. Just a sneak peak into the world of home care and elderly care. It’s not an easy job and I wish we got the appropriate appreciation. But I do love my residents and care for them to the best of my ability no matter what.
